items.justification: Both mandate secure software development processes including version control; A adds compiler hardening for device software, B adds asset tracking and authentication for AI assets.
Critical security parameter lifecycle management is a different objective from threat modelling triggered by configuration changes, and B's process text does not name key management.
Both require informing users about security risks so they can act; A covers update notices, B covers unresolved threats passed down the stakeholder chain.
Sensor transparency and update notification are different objectives; only the phrase "accessible way" is shared.
Both require notifying users ahead of an update; A adds the mitigated risks, B adds prior notice of model changes specifically.
Both pursue user-facing transparency about update status; A covers devices that receive none, B covers those that do.
In-house development processes and contractual flow-down to cloud providers jointly serve securing the software supply chain.
Both enable authenticity verification of distributed software artefacts; A by unique per-device parameters, B by published cryptographic hashes.
Both protect sensitive data proportionately to its properties; A mandates transit encryption, B mandates usage and controls matched to data sensitivity.
Recording justifications for unmet recommendations and risk-assessing external components are distinct steps of one documented risk management process.
Timely vulnerability remediation and post-incident user support are distinct duties combining into coordinated vulnerability and incident handling.
External component due diligence does not name key or parameter management, and the two obligations share no objective.
Validating inbound data and restricting outbound permissions are different objectives that jointly secure a system's interfaces to other systems.
Both require accessible publication of security support information; A the support period, B the individual security updates.
Per-device key uniqueness and least-privilege permissions between systems pursue unrelated objectives.
Hardware memory access control and API rate limiting address different attack surfaces with no shared control.
Both serve authenticity of software assets; A through unique per-device parameters, B through processes and tools that authenticate assets.
Secure development practice and the security content of the accompanying documentation are distinct parts of one secure development lifecycle.
Detecting unauthorized software change on a device is unrelated to rate-limiting an external API.
Documenting sensors and publishing a disclosure policy are different obligations sharing only the act of publication.
Runtime verification of update artefacts differs from design-time verification that specified controls were implemented.
Both require contingency for the case where an update cannot be applied; A through recovery to a known good state, B through documented mitigation plans.
Both demand assurance over externally sourced components before use; A by requiring reviewed implementations, B by requiring risk assessment and due diligence.
Both require documented, risk-based justification of design decisions; A for unmet recommendations, B for the decision to build the system at all.
General adversarial robustness of an AI system does not relate specifically to per-device uniqueness of update keys.
Patching promptly and communicating threats that cannot be patched are distinct duties within one vulnerability handling process.
Both pursue continuous identification of security weaknesses; A by supplier monitoring, B by encouraging internal reporting.
Publishing the support period and publishing the disclosure policy are distinct commitments that together make a supplier's security posture public.
Supply chain process requirements do not name key or parameter management, which is the whole subject of A.
Both require maintenance and support plans to be documented and made available; A to users, B to downstream operators.
User interface input validation and verification of implemented controls pursue different objectives.
A informs end users about a pending update; B trains staff on threat awareness. Different obligations on different parties.
Both centre on threat modelling to identify and mitigate risks; A demands justification records, B demands regular reviews and named AI attack classes.
Monitoring and rectifying vulnerabilities and planning for when they cannot be fixed are distinct halves of lifecycle vulnerability management.
Sensor documentation and advance notice of model updates share only the accessibility wording.
Automatic update activation and recovery is a device mechanism; incident support to affected entities is an organizational duty with a different objective.
A general risk assessment duty for external model components does not name key management, which is A's subject.
B's logging duty explicitly names vulnerability remediation as the activity it supports, which is exactly the activity A mandates.
Secure coding training is a general process provision whose text does not name key management.
Notifying users of a required update is a different objective from specifying the security content of system documentation.
